say: You sleep six hours, drink coffee after dinner, scroll in bed until midnight, and then you wonder why you're always tired.
All day, a chemical builds up in your brain and makes you sleepy, and sleep is the cleaning crew that clears it out.
Cut the night short, and some of yesterday's mess is still there in the morning.
Coffee doesn't clean any of it.
It just hides the signal, like tape over a warning light.
Drink it at six in the evening, and about half of it is still in you at eleven.
Maybe you're not a light sleeper. Maybe you're just caffeinated.
Your body was built to run on the sun, so even an ordinary lamp or a screen at night makes your body clock think it's still daytime, and your sleep hormone shows up late.
Your alarm, sadly, still shows up on time.
So for a seven a.m. alarm, be in bed by eleven, stop coffee by two, and dim the lights from eight.
If you're still exhausted after that, or it comes with fever, sweats or weight loss you can't explain, see a doctor.
If you feel confused or dizzy, or have thoughts of harming yourself, get help straight away.
Let's get you back to factory settings.
